newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors say Hamanaka got cash from Winchester.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors say Hamanaka got cash from Winchester.

text.p: Japanese prosecutors said on Monday that former Sumitomo Corp copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka received about 15 million yen as a "gratitude payment" from a U.K.-based commodities trading group.

The statement from the Tokyo prosecutors office did not specify what the money was in gratitude for, but said that Hamanaka, who earlier pleaded guilty to charges of fraud and forgery in relation to unauthorised trading, had made extensive transactions through Winchester and its Tokyo office.
The statement said that Hamanaka received the money between the autumn of 1992 and the spring of 1993.

It said the Winchester Tokyo representative was a close acquaintance of Hamanaka and since he opened the Tokyo office in 1992, Hamanaka had used it as a broker and a go-between for some of Sumitomo"s dealings on the London Metal Exchange.
Hamanaka spent the money he received from Winchester on golf club memberships, entertaining clients at night clubs, overseas travel and other forms of entertainment, it said.
Hamanaka entered the guilty pleas at the start of his trial at the Tokyo District Court on charges of forgery and fraud. The charges carry a penalty of up to 15 years in prison.
Hamanaka was fired last June by Sumitomo for what it said were years of unauthorised trading. The company estimates the improper trading cost the firm $2.6 billion.
Winchester at that time said it was in no way responsible for Sumitomo"s losses and said it had minimal involvement with Sumitomo during the 12 months preceding its statement.

The Financial Times on Monday reported that investigations by BBC television"s Panorama programme, to be aired on Monday, found that a complex copper deal involving both companies, code-named RADR, was "unfairly priced" in Winchester"s favour.
In its statement last June, Winchester said "The RADR transaction was known of and approved by a board member of Sumitomo."
